You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-cmds):
- file: driver/cmd_doctor.cpp:175
- category: duplication
- title: read_hybrid_toolchain hand-rolls a second config.env parser; the same key is resolved elsewhere via config_env_value
- detail: cmd_doctor.cpp carries ~45 lines of private config.env parsing (strip_char at line 41, parse_toolchain_line at 146, read_hybrid_toolchain at 175) just to resolve HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, while the same binary already resolves the SAME key with the shared helper config_env_value("HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN") in manifest.cpp:86 and cmd_profile.cpp:76 (config_env.hpp:22). The two parsers diverge: doctor's accepts `export KEY = "value"` (optional export keyword, whitespace around '=', double-then-single quote stripping), config_env_value accepts only plain `KEY=value`. So today doctor can report the toolchain PASS from an `export`-style line that `--runtime linux` staging and `profile` then fail to resolve. The comment at line 145 says it "mirrors hsim._read_hybrid_toolchain" -- the deleted Python driver (no *hsim* files exist in the repo), confirming this is a carried-over port, and config_env.hpp:5's own comment claims it matches "how cmd_doctor already resolves HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN", which is no longer exactly true. Collapse to one parser: replace read_hybrid_toolchain's file branch with config_env_value("HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN") and delete strip_char/parse_toolchain_line.
- claimed safety: On the documented config.env format (plain KEY=value; config.env.example line 13 ships exactly that, no export/quotes) both parsers return identical values, so doctor's rows are unchanged. Behavior differs only for export/quoted lines -- inputs the binary's other two consumers of the same key already cannot parse, so unifying makes doctor consistent rather than silently more permissive. If byte-exact preservation on exotic lines is required, the alternative is hoisting doctor's permissive parser into config_env.hpp for all three callers; either way the duplicate parser goes away.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

# Hybrid simulator per-host configuration.
#
# This file is the TEMPLATE (committed). On first `source ./setup.sh`,
# it is copied to ./config.env (gitignored). Edit ./config.env to point
# at the toolchain on your host; never commit your local edits.
#
# Both setup.sh and the test harness scripts load ./config.env at
# startup, so an exported value in your shell takes precedence; this
# file fills in the gaps when something runs without prior `source`.

# Andes RISC-V GCC + libgloss_vh toolchain root. Must contain
# bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}.
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/home/nick/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d

# The rv32 toolchain root (separate install), for rv32 runtime/fixture builds.
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds32le-elf-newlib-v5d

# Andes RISC-V glibc/Linux-ABI toolchain root (rv64), ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md
# U4+. Must contain bin/riscv64-linux-{gcc,g++,ld,...}. Static-linked test
# fixtures only -- vlinux implements no dynamic loader.
LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d

# llama.cpp checkout root, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U8+. Needs a static
# riscv64 build (see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11) at
# $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion, and a GGUF model
# at $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (or override both via
# LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN / BONSAI_GGUF). Leave unset if you are not working
# on the llama.cpp-under-vlinux effort -- tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh
# skips cleanly without it.
LLAMA_CPP_DIR=/home/nick/work/llama.cpp

# QEMU build dir (external prebuilt qemu-system-*); added for the external-QEMU migration.
QEMU_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/build/qemu

# vsim build dir (external prebuilt sim_*); added for the external-vsim migration.
VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build
---exit 0
